measure_name: Spatiotemporal overlap of wild-duck utilization distributions (UDs) and HPAI H5N1 poultry outbreaks
what_it_represents: The wild duck–infected poultry transmission interface, represented by poultry outbreaks occurring within tracked duck home-range utilization distributions relative to outbreaks outside those distributions.
measurement_method: Satellite telemetry data were used to generate 14-day, three-dimensional UDs; poultry outbreak data were compared inside versus outside each UD, within a minimum convex polygon (MCP), using 1-sample exact binomial tests.
metric_or_unit: Number and proportion of poultry outbreaks inside versus outside UDs by 14-day period; percentage of UDs significantly associated with poultry outbreaks.
role_in_analysis: Tested whether poultry outbreaks overlapped duck UDs more than expected from the relative UD area within the MCP, and compared overlap by season and species.
quantitative_result: During the spring migration, a larger proportion of the utilization distributions of both Common Teal (23.1%) and Common Shelduck (27.3%) significantly overlapped with H5N1-infected poultry.
evidence_quote: During the spring migration, a larger proportion of the utilization distributions of both Common Teal (23.1%) and Common Shelduck (27.3%) significantly overlapped with H5N1-infected poultry (Supplementary Table S6).
section: 3.6 Duck–poultry interface: effect of season and species
